findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice long questions for Chapter 4 in the same format as the Physics chapter practice, long questions in the Computer Science Board shape (8 marks each) (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 22 questions numbered 1-22; by section: 4.1.1.2 1, 4.1.1.3 1, 4.1.2.1~2 1, 4.1.3.1 2, 4.1.3.2 1, 4.1.3.4 1, 4.1.3.5 1, 4.1.4.1 1, 4.1.5 1, 4.1.5.2 1, 4.1.6.1 2, 4.1.7.1 1, 4.1.7.2 1, 4.1.7.2~2 1, 4.1.8 1, 4.1.8.3 1, 4.1.8.4 1, 4.2 1, 4.3.2 1, 4.3.4 1.

Covers list properties and operations, stack push and pop (browser Back program), the three notations, infix to postfix and postfix evaluation traces, a balanced-parentheses program, an undo program, queue properties and a task-scheduling program, uses of queues, a BFS trace, tree properties and the FamilyTree program, traversal traces, balanced, binary and AVL trees, uses of trees, graphs (definition, tree vs graph, properties, types, operations), choosing a structure, a DFS trace and list reversal with a stack. The exercise's long questions are not repeated. Every program was run in Python 3 and its real output is given. Book corrections followed (insert(), append(), pop(), index(), q.get(), corrected FamilyTree program, prefix +AB, Notepad, Figure 4.10 with 15 on the left).
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
